records.name: South Kensington Community Partners, Inc.
records.summary: A community organization named by the City as a Neighborhood Advisory Committee, South Kensington Community Partners, Inc. connects neighbors in the Lower North part of the city with City services and a say in local priorities. It is also a registered community organization, so developers are asked to talk with it about nearby zoning and building plans.
records.what_you_do: Work with neighbors and the City on local services and what the area needs.

locations.label: Contact address (City list)
locations.address: 1525 N American Street, Studio #107, Philadelphia, PA 19122

first_step.how: Email info@southkensingtoncommunity.org to volunteer or to ask about joining one of the five neighbor-led committees, then subscribe to the weekly email newsletter for events.
first_step.basis: The site invites any neighbor to join a committee or to volunteer by email, and says you can stop by the office on weekdays. No page uses the word newcomer or beginner.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not post committee meeting times, so an email is the best first step. The office keeps weekday hours of 9 am to 5 pm. The committees cover business outreach, fundraising, greening, a neighborhood advisory subcommittee, and planning and zoning. The site does not mention a fee to take part.
first_visit_tips: Email first, because no meeting dates or times are posted on the site.
On a weekday between 9 am and 5 pm you can stop by the office at 1525 N American Street, Studio 107.
Ask which committee needs help right now and when it next meets.
Sign up for the weekly newsletter to hear about events before you come.

records.notes: Office hours (Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm) are printed on the contact page. That page lists two unlabeled addresses: 1525 N American Street (Ray Philly), Studio 107, kept as the office, and 1301 N 2nd St, not added as a location. Committee meeting times are not posted. The newest dated item on the site is the 2025 year end fundraiser, so status and last_sign_of_life are tier 1 values (City registry), not confirmed by the site.

records.name: Strawberry Mansion Neighborhood Action Center
records.summary: Strawberry Mansion CDC is a neighborhood nonprofit, founded in 2004, that works on home repair, neighborhood land care, and job help for young adults. Its Neighborhood Action Center is also listed by the City as a local advisory group for the Lower North area.
records.what_you_do: Help with phone or in-person outreach, event tabling, or grant writing, or take part in the monthly Zoom call on local work.

schedule.text: Monthly Call to Action meeting on Zoom, 6 to 7:30 pm.

first_step.how: Join the monthly Call to Action meeting on Zoom, 6 to 7:30 pm, through the link on the event page, and use the RSVP button if you plan to come.
first_step.basis: The monthly meeting is open to the community on Zoom, and the volunteer form is public. No page says newcomers are welcome by name.
first_step.what_to_expect: The monthly call focuses on the Outdoor Leadership Program run with Philadelphia Outward Bound School. It is aimed at anyone who wants to join the conversation about the neighborhood, and the event page does not mention a fee. If you want to volunteer instead, the online form lets you pick phone outreach, in-person outreach, event tabling, or grant writing, and the group then contacts you.
first_visit_tips: Open the event page before the call to get the Zoom link and the RSVP button.
Plan for an evening, since the call runs 6 to 7:30 pm.
Check the Events page for one time gatherings such as community dinners.
To volunteer, fill in the online form on the Volunteer page and name the areas that interest you.

records.notes: Name question for review: the City list name is the Neighborhood Action Center, which the CDC site lists as one of its programs. The CDC calls itself Strawberry Mansion CDC (founded 2004). The tier 1 name is kept for now. The site publishes info@strawberrymansioncdc.org and 215-235-7505, while tier 1 email is on a different domain; tier 1 email is kept. The Oct 18 Fairmount Food Forest dinner is a one time event and is kept out of the schedule. The site job board link goes to a placeholder page and was not used. The footer copyright year is not evidence of activity.

records.name: Community Schools @Frankford High School
records.summary: A Community School partnership between the City, the School District and neighbors, Frankford High School welcomes volunteers through the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help hand out weekly groceries, keep the in-school food pantry going, help at school events such as resource fairs, or mentor students.

first_step.how: Contact the school's Community Schools office at (215) 834-6277, or email the address on the City listing, to ask how to start the clearances before you can volunteer.
first_step.basis: A volunteer must get several state and federal clearances before helping, so a first visit is paperwork rather than a walk-in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Before you can help inside the building, expect paperwork: the City listing asks volunteers for a school district code of conduct and certificate, state and federal background checks, and a City release waiver. Once cleared, volunteers help hand out weekly groceries, keep the in-school pantry going, help at school events, or mentor students. Hours and any fee are not in the record we hold.
first_visit_tips: Start the clearances early, since you need them before you can volunteer.
Ask the coordinator which role fits your schedule before you fill in the forms.
The school is at 5000 Oxford Avenue in the Frankford neighborhood, so check your route before you go.
Check the City volunteer listing for the full list of forms before you start.

records.notes: The City volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 in this pass, so requirements, what_you_do, what_to_expect and first_step rest on the tier 1 read of that listing and were not re-verified. Status and last_sign_of_life are also tier 1 values. The tier 1 what_to_expect held copied listing text; it is replaced here with our own words. The district Frankford High School page (philasd.org/frankford) was read: it covers a 2025 ribbon cutting for the reopened main building and does not describe volunteers, so it is not cited for any field. The district Community Schools page returned HTTP 404. Newest dated item seen: an August 18, 2025 district article, older than the tier 1 date, so it did not change status.

records.name: Frankford CDC
records.summary: Frankford CDC is a community development group in Lower Northeast Philadelphia. It works on small business help, affordable and workforce housing, job programs, and keeping vacant lots and corridors clean. The City also lists it as a neighborhood advisory group.
records.what_you_do: The group runs business, housing, workforce, and public space programs in Lower Northeast. The site does not list volunteer roles.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: 2nd Baptist Church, 1801 Meadow Street, Philadelphia, PA 19124

first_step.how: Call (215) 743-6580 or send a message through the contact form on frankfordcdc.org, and ask how to hear about upcoming workshops and volunteer needs.
first_step.basis: The site lists a phone line, a contact form, and a newsletter, but no meetings, volunteer roles, or visiting hours, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not list a regular meeting, volunteer shift, or visiting hours, so a first step is a call or a message. Its events calendar showed no events for October 2026 when we checked. The group runs business, housing, workforce, and public space programs, and its office is on the second floor of the Daral Building. The site does not mention a fee for these services.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead or send a message first, since no visiting hours are posted.
The office is on the second floor of the Daral Building, 4667 to 4669 Paul Street, Philadelphia 19124.
Ask whether a business, housing, or job program fits what you need.
Sign up for the newsletter to hear about workshops and events.

records.notes: Status review needed: the newest dated item on the group's own site is a 2025 annual report with no month printed, the news page shows no dated items, and the events calendar was empty for October 2026. Status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10 are tier 1 values from the City registry, which records registration rather than activity. The site lists info@frankfordcdc.org while tier 1 email is kept. The 3rd Annual Community Heroes Breakfast is listed with a ticket link and no date, so it is not recorded as a schedule item. The 2nd Baptist Church meeting place comes from the City list, not the site.

records.name: Juniata Park Civic Association
records.summary: Juniata Park Civic Association is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the Lower Northeast part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Juniata Park Boys and Girls Club, 1001 E. Cayuga Street, Philadelphia, PA 19124

first_step.how: Email or call the contact on the City list to confirm when the next meeting is and whether the Boys and Girls Club is still the meeting place.
first_step.basis: No current meeting time or welcome page could be found. The only web address on file is a Facebook group, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: We could not find a current meeting schedule or a description of a typical meeting. The group's listed work is reviewing nearby building and zoning proposals and sharing its view with the City and developers. Confirm the date, time, and place before you go, since we found no fee information.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the next meeting by email or phone first.
Bring a specific building or zoning question if you have one, since that is the group's main work.
The only web address on file is a Facebook group, so do not rely on it alone for dates.

Two public articles about this group were refused with HTTP 403 and were not read (see blocked). A search snippet described an older 2017 profile with a second Tuesday monthly meeting; that came only from the snippet, so it is not used in any field. No dated item from 2018 or later was readable, so the active status and 2026-10 date are tier 1 City registry values. Review before publishing.

records.name: Lawncrest Community Association
records.summary: Lawncrest Community Association is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the Lower Northeast part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: St William's Social Hall, 6200 Rising Sun Avenue, Enter Hall corner of Robbins and Argyle Streets

first_step.how: Call or email the contact on the City list to ask when the next meeting is and whether a neighbor can attend as a visitor.
first_step.basis: No current meeting time or welcome page was found. The only web address on file is a Facebook group, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: We could not find a current meeting time for this group. The City list gives St. William's Social Hall at 6200 Rising Sun Avenue as the meeting place, but we could not confirm it is still used. The group's listed work is reviewing nearby zoning and building proposals, and we found no fee information.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before you go, since no current meeting time was found.
The City list says to enter the hall at the corner of Robbins and Argyle Streets.
Ask whether the meetings are open to neighbors who are not members.

records.notes: No group-owned website: the only web address is a Facebook group, which is lead-only and was not read. A WHYY article dated September 16, 2009 (https://whyy.org/articles/lawncrest-civic-association/) was read: it describes Tuesday night meetings, board members presenting zoning updates, and the group hosting candidates. It does not say whether the group is nonpartisan. Hosting candidates does not by itself make a group partisan, but a scope reviewer should check. The newest readable dated item is from 2009, so the active status and 2026-10 date are tier 1 City registry values. Review before publishing. records.name: Central Roxborough Civic Association (CRCA)
records.summary: Central Roxborough Civic Association (CRCA) is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the Lower Northwest part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

schedule.text: First Thursday of the month, September to June, 7:30 pm (doors open 7 pm). Most meetings are on Zoom.

locations.label: In-person meetings (two or three a year)
locations.address: St. Timothy's Episcopal Church, 5720 Ridge Ave

locations.label: Next in-person meeting
locations.address: Wolcoff Auditorium, Roxborough Memorial Hospital, 5800 Ridge Ave

cost.text: Yearly membership dues: $15 individual, $25 household, $50 business (raised in December 2024). Donations of any amount are also accepted.

first_step.how: Attend the next monthly meeting on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 7:30 pm (doors open 7 pm), in Wolcoff Auditorium at Roxborough Memorial Hospital.
first_step.basis: Monthly meetings invite neighbors to join, and the group publishes a mailing list and a contact address. The site does not use the words newcomer or beginner.
first_step.what_to_expect: A meeting opens with approval of the last meeting's minutes, then works through the agenda. The November 2026 agenda includes two zoning appeals. Visitors can follow the discussion and bring feedback on land use, zoning, safety, and sustainability, and detailed minutes are posted afterward. The site does not say a fee is needed to attend.
first_visit_tips: Arrive by 7 pm, when doors open, to find your seat before the 7:30 start.
Enter off Rector Street, to the left of the emergency entrance, or from Jamestown Street.
Read the minutes and the agenda on the site before you come.
Most meetings are on Zoom and the site does not print a link, so email the group before a Zoom meeting.

records.notes: Dues come from the join page and were raised in December 2024. The November 5, 2026 meeting is in person at Wolcoff Auditorium, which the site says differs from the usual in-person venue at St. Timothy's Episcopal Church. The site prints no Zoom link and no volunteer sign-up. The site lists info@crca.us as its contact, while tier 1 email centralroxrco@crca.us is kept. Entrance directions match the site text.
